record.paper_title: The cosmological constant, dark matter, supersymmetry, and other unsolved problems from a fresh perspective
record.original_question: What determines the values of the fundamental gauge coupling constant g0 and the gravitational coupling constant G, given that this would require a detailed understanding of very complex vacuum fields after multiple symmetry breakings at various energy scales?

evidence.quote: the values of the fundamental gauge and gravitational

coupling constants, g0 and G, which in the present theory would require a detailed understanding of the very complex vacuum fields after multiple symmetry breakings at various energy scales. These problems are all challenging, but the present picture does not appear to be inconsistent with potential solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Within a unified field-theoretic framework in which all known interactions arise from a single underlying theory with a hierarchy of spontaneous symmetry breakings at successively lower energy scales, determine, from first principles, the numerical values of the fundamental dimensionless gauge coupling constant g_0 (the unified gauge coupling defined at the highest unification scale, before any symmetry breaking) and the gravitational coupling constant G (Newton's constant, equivalently expressed as the dimensionless ratio G m_p^2/ħc using the proton mass m_p, or as the inverse square of the Planck mass). Specifically: starting from a Lagrangian invariant under the full unbroken symmetry group, characterize the vacuum field configurations resulting from the cascade of symmetry breakings at the various intermediate energy scales, and derive closed-form expressions or predicted numerical values for g_0 and G in terms of parameters of the unbroken theory. Show whether these values are uniquely fixed by consistency of the vacuum structure, or whether they remain free parameters.
artifact.category_tag: Fundamental coupling constants and symmetry breaking
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the values of the fundamental gauge and gravitational coupling constants from first principles is a long-standing open problem in theoretical physics. No accepted derivation exists; the values are taken as empirical inputs in the Standard Model and general relativity, and proposed approaches via grand unification, string theory, or anthropic reasoning remain unproven.

status_evidence.title: Coupling constant - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The values of the fundamental coupling constants of the Standard Model are not predicted by the theory and must be determined experimentally.
status_evidence.claim: The values of g_0 and G are not derivable from current accepted theory and are empirical inputs.

status_evidence.title: Dimensionless physical constant - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: There is no currently accepted theory that explains the values of the dimensionless fundamental physical constants.
status_evidence.claim: Explaining values of fundamental dimensionless constants remains open.
